summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at RIT (May 2026) with bare-metal firmware on ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32), FreeRTOS device driver design, and real-time Edge AI deployment (TensorRT/C++) on NVIDIA Jetson; academic background in Digital Signal Processing and Electronics & Telecommunication.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter via software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank for noise suppression achieving PSNR of 86; built optimized signal processing pipeline targeting memory-constrained inspection hardware.
Architected a metal surface inspection system using image stitching, wavelet denoising, and monocular depth estimation for microscopic crack profiling.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member team across national-level competitions owning PCB fabrication, firmware integration, and AI/ML deployment end-to-end.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret — STM32 + Jetson Edge AI
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending real-time control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and interrupt-driven UART command handling.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C device driver on ARM Cortex-M4.
Programmed peripherals in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated TensorRT YOLO (~18 FPS) and VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C mux on Jetson; implemented two-link IK in C++ on Arduino for contact-aware grasping.
Achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency after resolving 11 firmware and integration failures.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
